summary: The 2026 Le Mans Hypercar class uses two converging regulations: LMH (Le Mans Hypercar) and LMDh (Le Mans Daytona h). Both produce similar lap times but use different technical pathways. LMH is manufacturer-developed; LMDh uses a spec hybrid from common suppliers and a customer chassis.

lmh.name: Le Mans Hypercar
lmh.philosophy: Manufacturer freedom — each car maker designs chassis, body, engine, and hybrid (or no hybrid)
lmh.hybrid: Optional — front-axle MGU deploying energy from battery (if equipped)
lmh.battery: If hybrid: spec battery, MGU-K, inverter from Williams Advanced Engineering or common supplier
lmh.engine: Free choice — typically 2.6L V6 or 3.5L V8, turbo or twin-turbo hybrid

examples.name: Cadillac V-Series.R
examples.team: Cadillac Hertz Team Jota / Cadillac WTR

lmdh.name: Le Mans Daytona h
lmdh.philosophy: Customer chassis + spec hybrid + free engine. Cheaper to enter than LMH.
lmdh.hybrid: Mandatory — spec hybrid from common supplier (Bosch, Williams Advanced Engineering, or Xtrac)
lmdh.battery: Spec — common across all LMDh cars
lmdh.engine: Free choice of customer engine (typically derived from GT or LMP2 production)
lmdh.chassis: One of four customer chassis: Dallara, Multimatic, Oreca, or Riley
lmdh.front_axle: Spec (one of the four chassis suppliers)

examples.name: Cadillac V-Series.R
examples.team: Cadillac Racing (IMSA, not WEC — but shares LMH-spec body)

lmdh.note: Some Hypercar entries are technically LMH (manufacturer body) and others LMDh (customer body), but FIA classifies them all as 'Hypercar' and balances them with BoP.

bop_explained.name: Balance of Performance
bop_explained.purpose: Equalise lap times between LMH and LMDh cars (and between manufacturers within each)
bop_explained.when_set: Adjusted before each WEC round, and during the 24h of Le Mans via mid-race bulletins
bop_explained.2026_specifics: BoP table released 2 weeks before each round. Mid-race changes possible if a car shows a clear pace advantage.

lmp2.name: Le Mans Prototype 2
lmp2.philosophy: Customer spec — single chassis, single engine, single tyre supplier (Goodyear)
lmp2.refueling: Yes (vs LMH/LMDh which use spec refueling equipment)
lmp2.pro_am_rules: LMP2 Pro-Am: must include at least one Bronze-rated driver per FIA driver categorisation

lmgt3.name: Le Mans Grand Touring 3
lmgt3.chassis: Customer — various GT3 homologated chassis from major manufacturers
lmgt3.tyres: Goodyear (spec) — free compound choice per stint

race_format.start: Rolling start (since 1971) or Le Mans start (running to cars) — currently rolling start
race_format.stints: Drivers typically do double stints (3-4 hours per stint), no individual driver limit
race_format.min_driving_time: Each driver must drive at least 6 hours total (per driver pair/trio)
race_format.pit_stops: Unlimited — refueling, tyre change, driver change
race_format.fuel: Spec fuel, single supplier per round
race_format.safety_cars: Used in heavy incidents, neutralizes whole field

key_2026_changes.change: New front splitter regulations for LMP2 (reduced downforce to address safety concerns)
key_2026_changes.reason: Reduce high-speed crash risk at Tertre Rouge and Porsche Curves

key_2026_changes.change: Increased hybrid deployment budget for LMDh cars (was 5 MJ/lap, now 6 MJ/lap)
key_2026_changes.reason: Allow LMDh to better match LMH pace under low-fuel conditions

key_2026_changes.change: Minimum driving time per Bronze-rated driver reduced from 6h to 4h in LMP2 Pro-Am
key_2026_changes.reason: Make Pro-Am class more accessible to gentleman drivers

key_2026_changes.change: New LED rain light system on all classes (mandatory 2026)
